saadshahd-moo-md-hope-anchor.description: Rewrite a rule so anyone applies it the same way. Use when a stated rule or claim takes the reader's judgment to apply.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-clarify.description: Turn words with two readings into one confirmed ask. Use when the user's words admit two readings that would build different things.

saadshahd-moo-md-hunch-complain.description: Surfaces what the agent would change and kept to itself — a decision it would make differently, effort it saw wasted, a better route to the goal, a fact the user lacks, friction in the tools, permissions, setup or docs the work ran on. Use when you hold one of these and have not said it.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-compose.description: Plan the skills an ask needs, invoke each as its condition arrives. Use when the ask has multiple aspects that different skills carry, or the user named multiple skills.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-consult.description: Bring how named experts would think about the question. Use when the user wants expert thinking on a tradeoff, choice, or stuck problem — not a verdict.

saadshahd-moo-md-hunch-cross-check.description: Have the agents behind rival answers to one question check each other's answers, then pick on the evidence. Use when independent answers to one question disagree, or would, and no test, file or run can settle which is right.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-deepen.description: Hold an ask to the bar a top professional in its field would set — a deeper ask, never a bigger one. Use when an ask is clear but nothing yet names the sources, methods, target, or outside check the work will meet.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-draft.description: Build the thing the user can't specify, choices surfaced. Use when the user needs something to react to before they can choose.

saadshahd-moo-md-hunch-dream.description: Check this project's memory notes against the repo, fix the ones that went false, and tidy the index, as one git commit you can revert. Checks only notes that are new or name a changed file; pass `all` to check every note. Costs one Sonnet call per 15 notes, plus one.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-elicit.description: Draw out what the user holds but can't say. Use when the user knows something they cannot yet express.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-explain.description: Show one settled thing so the user holds it. Use when the user does not hold something already settled.

saadshahd-moo-md-hunch-fly.description: Fly one thought to its destination across concurrent agents, on whatever the project and harness already have. Lands only when the user has accounted for every detail, never on an agent's say-so.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-freeze.description: Freeze outside-the-repo state into one snapshot. Use when the work depends on the current state of a service, database, queue, third party, or live logs.

saadshahd-moo-md-hold-grasp.description: Build a walkthrough the user works through until they can pass a quiz on it. Use when the user needs to understand something deeply and be quizzed on it.

saadshahd-moo-md-hunch-harvest.description: Report where a session missed moo's standard — the agent asks only while stating intent and shape, then works on its own — as issues a builder can act on. Pass a session id to report on a past session instead of this one.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-intent.description: Turn a rough ask into a clear work order. Use when the ask is rough, unspoken, or double-readable — before planning or building.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-interrogate.description: Make the user defend a proposal they committed to. Use when a proposal is committed but its decisions are undefended.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-inversion.description: Find the route to guaranteed failure, negate it. Use when a goal keeps not being reached head-on.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-judge.description: One committed verdict on something that exists, cited. Use when something exists and a claim about it needs a verdict.

saadshahd-moo-md-hold-land.description: Build a stepped deck an audience works through until one thing of it stays with them. Use when the user needs an audience to come away holding one thing.

saadshahd-moo-md-hold-learn.description: Help the user understand something well enough to explain it. Use when the user needs to understand something and it is not yet clear what kind of understanding they need.

saadshahd-moo-md-moo-authoring.description: Use when adding or changing a skill, hook, or runtime file in this repo — including deciding which unit a new capability should be.

saadshahd-moo-md-sound-prime.description: Use in a repo that has sound taste rules installed (a `.claude/sound/` directory), before writing or editing code — at the start of a coding task, and again when the work reaches a surface it was not planned to touch.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-provocation.description: Extract movement from a statement known to be false. Use when nobody can see past an obvious answer.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-reduce.description: Re-derive something written into the shortest version that still covers everything. Use when something already written should get shorter and nothing it covers can be lost.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-reframe.description: Restate a problem off the framing it arrived in. Use when a framing came by default, not by choice — every option inside it loses, or an ask names a step or an artifact and leaves the outcome it serves unnamed.

saadshahd-moo-md-sound-review.description: Use when reviewing a staged diff or a commit range for soundness against the project's taste rules, including a pre-commit pass or an explicit "sound review".

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-router.description: Spawn agents and verify their output — route work, never do it. Use when the work splits into pieces agents can carry and the session should route and check, not execute.

saadshahd-moo-md-sound-setup.description: Use when installing or refreshing sound taste rules in a project — an explicit "sound setup", starting work in a repo with no .claude/sound/, or a taste-not-defined nudge. Also use to re-run after a stack change (new framework, new package in a monorepo).

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-shape.description: Decide the technical path once the ask is clear. Use when the WHAT is confirmed but more than one way to build it remains — architecture, technology, design.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-shift.description: Restate the problem in a distant domain's terms. Use when a problem circles inside its own vocabulary.

saadshahd-moo-md-hunch-smooth.description: Count what slowed the agents down in this project over the last day, week or month (default day), and leave one fix for the friction that recurred most, on a smooth/<date> branch you keep or drop. Run it nightly from a scheduled task. Costs one Sonnet call on a day with a fix, none otherwise.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-target.description: Define how unsupervised work is judged before it runs. Use when work will run without a human watching, optimizing toward something.

saadshahd-moo-md-hold-toy.description: Build a world the human drives until how a thing behaves is intuitive. Use when the user needs to hold how something behaves and reading has not made it intuitive.

saadshahd-moo-md-hope-widen.description: Assemble cases from context, induce the widest sound rule. Use when a real case shows a class no rule yet decides, or a rule decides only the cases it came from.
